messages:
ashley (support): triaging an urgent customer escalation — multiple 5xx + consistent 30s+ timeouts against hosted inference since ~08:10 UTC. customer says spike started after a high-traffic campaign. they provided a curl snippet and example request IDs.

customer-rep: FYI customer saw 502s and 504s across regions (us-west1 and eu-west1). reported latency p95 jumped from ~120ms to >12s. they captured 'gateway timeout' and 'request_queue_full' messages in our SDK. :rotating_light:

ash (ops-bot): Automated alert: hosted-gateway.request_queue_depth > 950 (threshold 800) for 7m. continuous-batcher.backlog_length spiked to 4200. autoscaler action suppressed due to pool quota.

jordan (eng-runtime): copying logs from the gateway pool: 
```
[2026-03-15T08:12:03Z] gateway: warn: request_queue_enqueue failed: queue_depth_limit reached (len=1024,max=1024)
[2026-03-15T08:12:04Z] gateway: error: dispatch timeout -> early_reject 504
[2026-03-15T08:12:05Z] batcher: warn: continuous backlog=4230 pending_batches=67
[2026-03-15T08:12:06Z] model-host: info: worker 3 blocked on kv-cache load, inflight_tokens=4096
```

mike (infra): Looks like queue depth caps triggered early rejects. we had a quota on dedicated ephemeral pools for hosted free-tier scaling — hit the soft limit at 08:11. autoscaler didn't spin up because of a region capacity constraint (GPUs exhausted).

sara (oncall): Customer repro steps requested. Ashley — can you ask them for a minimal repro that consistently hits the tail? Also need sample request IDs and model name.

ash (ops-bot): Collected traces: trace_ids: [trc-1182, trc-1183, trc-1187]. Routing policy shows ~70% requests went to pool-canary-03 which had older kernel optimizations disabled.

ashley (support): Customer sent sample: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
{
  "model": "rw-large-ctx-32k",
  "prompt": "summarize: ... (large prompt ~10k chars)",
  "max_tokens": 1024
}
```
They say failures correlate with large prompts and high concurrency (50+ parallel threads).

jordan (eng-runtime): Hypothesis: long prefix + large max_tokens -> huge KV cache usage -> worker stalls -> batcher backlog forms -> queue depth fills -> gateway starts early rejecting. Also continuous batching configuration's max_batch_delay may be accumulating many requests into giant batches.

mike (infra): We can temporarily mitigate: 1) throttle per-tenant concurrency at the gateway (soft limit 20) 2) reduce continuous batching max delay from 10ms -> 3ms for the affected pool 3) shift traffic away from pool-canary-03 to stable pools. Any risk?

sara (oncall): Sounds reasonable. Do it with staged rollouts: implement throttling rule for the tenant, then reduce max delay on canary, then move 20% traffic off canary to give headroom. Coordinate with support to notify the customer.

jordan (eng-runtime): Action plan I'm going to run now: 
1) patch gateway to enforce tenant-level concurrency override for tenant T-438 (one-off) 
2) change continuous-batcher config on pool-canary-03: `max_batch_delay_ms: 3`, `max_batch_tokens: 2048` 
3) add temporary autoscaler override to allow burst +1 GPU if capacity frees up
Run commands: 
```
# enforce per-tenant concurrent requests
redctl route update --tenant T-438 --concurrency 20 --env hosted --pool pool-canary-03
# apply batcher tweak
redctl pool config set pool-canary-03 --continuous-batcher.max_batch_delay_ms=3
```

ash (ops-bot): Deploy started: gateway-policy-update (id d-2034), pool-config-update (id p-8493). Notifying customer.

ashley (support): sent customer heads-up and mitigation steps. asked them to throttle client-side and provide timings for any future failures. customer replied: "ok trying client-side cap at 20 concurrent, will report back in 10m".

[~6m later]

customer-rep: After cap at 20, error rate dropped dramatically. p95 returned to ~200ms. early_rejects stopped. Customer still sees occasional 5xx (1-2%) on very large prompts.

jordan (eng-runtime): We pulled more detailed heap/traces from pool-canary-03. Observed frequent GC pauses on model-host process when kv-cache miss storms happen for large prefixes. Those pauses were causing head-of-line blocking in the batcher.

mike (infra): Follow-up long-term items: 1) improve kv-cache eviction for large prompt patterns 2) add tenant adaptive concurrency controls built-in to gateway 3) adjust default continuous-batcher to be lower-latency for hosted multicore pools

sara (oncall): For post-incident: open a runbook entry (incidents -> runbooks -> queue-tail-degrade) and a customer incident summary. Ashley please draft the customer facing postmortem and cc account exec. Include reproduction steps and recommended SDK client-side throttling.

ash (ops-bot): Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Metrics to watch: hosted-gateway.request_queue_depth, continuous-batcher.backlog_length, model-host.kv_cache_miss_rate. Recommended alert: fire when queue_depth > 700 for 5m AND backlog_length > 500.

ashley (support): Customer acknowledged the mitigation and will schedule a follow-up to test with larger traffic after we roll kv-cache improvements. Closing loop with account team. :thumbsup:

sara (oncall): Marking this thread resolved for immediate escalation. Will leave open for the runbook + follow-ups. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
